## Implemented boundary

- The typed domain entity and application command preserve omitted, explicit
  null, blank, zero-like, and concrete scalar states where the contract
  distinguishes them.
- POST requires `address`; PUT also requires `address` while preserving
  omitted optional scalar and relationship state; PATCH preserves every
  omitted scalar.
- `status` defaults only on create omission. Null and blank status are
  rejected. Role create omission persists SQL `NULL`, while explicit null or
  blank clears to the baseline blank value.
- DNS name, description, and comments default only on create omission, reject
  null, accept blank clearing, and preserve omission on PUT/PATCH. Successful
  values retain the declared normalization rules.
- Address normalization covers maskless IPv4/IPv6 defaults, host-bit
  preservation, dotted netmask/hostmask forms, and bounded Python-compatible
  numeric suffix handling, including Unicode decimal digits.
- Choice conversion preserves the pinned baseline's numeric-to-character
  behavior, including negative zero, floating-point thresholds, and
  overflow/underflow classifications.
- Validation rejects embedded NUL, surrogate escapes, malformed UTF-8 bodies,
  and invalid address/choice inputs with stable field-scoped REST or
  transport-native gRPC errors. Every rejected mutation leaves the resource,
  timestamp, assignment, and object-change count unchanged.
- REST and gRPC map into the same application command semantics; real
  PostgreSQL proves durable parity. No schema, migration, bootstrap, registry,
  AutoMigrate, protobuf, or generated-Go boundary changed.
- Operation-specific generated OpenAPI now distinguishes POST, PUT, and PATCH
  required/null/blank rules. The resource validator adversarially rejects
  missing operation metadata, invalid subsets, duplicate/undeclared fields,
  response/write conflation, and stale request-schema references.
- Vue serializes untouched, cleared, blank, and concrete IPAddress form values
  distinctly, retains required Address/Status and optional Role/text metadata,
  and consumes field-scoped REST validation.

Identity behavior, IPAddress uniqueness, assignment-pair semantics,
reassignment, deletion, filters, ordering, permissions, empty-PATCH behavior,
and all other resources remain outside this increment.

## External differential and residual limits

The focused pinned-oracle differential did not run because the required
oracle, Go endpoint, and durable-artifact configuration were all absent. No
local transport test substitutes for that external boundary, so strict REST
differential proof and T2 remain pending.

The pinned source contains the anomalous expression
`_('Invalid IP address format: {data}').format(data)`, whose named placeholder
is supplied positionally. Without the executable oracle, this increment keeps
the Go boundary fail-closed with a hardened 400 response and does not claim the
exact malformed-input differential outcome. Python's runtime integer-string
conversion cap for inputs beyond 4,300 decimal digits also remains outside the
bounded lexical vectors proved here.
